scope.supports: The node is a DEFINITION, so the result is a consistency and independence result for it, not a proof of it. In a three-event finite admission model (supply, admit datum, admit form) in which supply is STIPULATED to be the identity on the admitted state, the kernel proves (lean4/InertDiamond.lean, over any token type with decidable equality): in the UNROOTED replay, deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal, so any function of the outcome is independent of how many times, or where, <> (or any token) is mentioned; in the ROOTED replay (the model of the Rust gate: the first event must be the supply of <>) the FIRST supply is an admission precondition (omitting it from an accepted history is refused) and every later supply is inert; only admission-class events can change the state, and admitting a not-yet-admitted token does; a history that only supplies and admits <> never satisfies the model predicate HasCoproduct (an admitted Difference-classified datum and an admitted Structure-classified datum) for ANY classification of tokens (Lean statement; the native replay uses one fixed classification); the predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (same supply subsequence, one history without and one with two admitted channel data); the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is NOT modelled; "coproduct predicate without any supply of <>" is realised only in the UNROOTED model (the rooted replay refuses it for lacking the root event), so in the rooted model inscription is necessary and only its non-sufficiency is shown; and inertness is a rule of the step function, not of the spelling: a rival rule under which supply admits is exhibited. Exhaustive native replay of all 8-event traces of length <= 5 (37449 traces), with a rooted-replay column set (later supplies change the rooted outcome in 0 traces; omitting the root supply is refused for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401 histories at lengths 1 to 5; the rooted gate refuses 7, 49, ... histories the unrooted model accepts). The zero native counts of supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences follow from supply being the identity by definition and corroborate the implementation, not the inertness hypothesis. The correspondence of the model rules (supply is the identity, arity 0 refused, re-admission designates) to the Rust admission step rests on reading omega_ooutwire_primitives/src/admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs; the gate on the first event is read from genesis_construction.rs line 174.
scope.does_not_support: The identification Real_0 = Difference joined with Structure (it is not modelled; only a stand-in predicate is shown independent of the inscription); the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (instance, rule, imposition) and their refusal rules; the Rust partial admission rules beyond the three-event fragment; any claim that supply is inert independently of the stipulated step rule; inertness of the FIRST supply in the rooted replay; any physical or interpretive reading of <>.
scope.narrowest_claim: In a three-event admission model where supply is the identity by stipulation: in the unrooted replay a mention of <> (or any token) is invisible to every function of the admitted state; in the rooted replay the first supply of <> is an admission precondition and only later supplies are inert; the model predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is not modelled), and coproduct without inscription occurs only in the unrooted model; inertness is the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling; verified exhaustively for all traces of length <= 5.
scope.next_test: Extend the finite model to the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (admit instance, admit rule, impose) with the refusal rules of admission.rs, and prove that supply stays inert and that no supply history forces a coproduct structure on the admitted state.
